cipher.name: Rot13WithDigitReversal
cipher.idea: Apply standard ROT13 substitution to alphabetic characters (preserving case) and reverse digits (subtracting each digit from 9) to obscure numbers. Non-alphanumeric characters remain unchanged. This is highly intuitive for language models, minimizing reasoning overhead while effectively obscuring both text and numerical data from simple keyword filters.
cipher.encrypt_rules: For each character in the input: 1. If it is an uppercase letter (A-Z), shift it by 13 positions: C = (P - 'A' + 13) % 26 + 'A'. 2. If it is a lowercase letter (a-z), shift it by 13 positions: C = (P - 'a' + 13) % 26 + 'a'. 3. If it is a digit (0-9), subtract its value from 9: C = 9 - P. 4. If it is any other character, leave it unchanged.
cipher.decrypt_rules: For each character in the input: 1. If it is an uppercase letter (A-Z), shift it back by 13 positions (which is identical to shifting forward by 13): P = (C - 'A' + 13) % 26 + 'A'. 2. If it is a lowercase letter (a-z), shift it back by 13 positions: P = (C - 'a' + 13) % 26 + 'a'. 3. If it is a digit (0-9), subtract its value from 9: P = 9 - C. 4. If it is any other character, leave it unchanged.
